messages:
alex: Quick summary from the postmortem yesterday: we saw a sustained burst of DNS retry loops that triggered cross-region LB failovers between us-east and us-west on 2026-03-19. Root cause appears to be a combination of short DNS TTLs, intermittent NXDOMAIN responses from our registrar, and the GSLB health-check logic treating transient NX as unhealthy.

priya: Agreed. We also saw a higher-than-normal SYN timeouts for TLS handshakes during the failover window.

ben: Noted. I'm tracking the metrics — exports attached to the postmortem doc: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-19-dns-retries

julia: Proposed action items (from f2f):
1) Short-term: tighten GSLB health-check debounce (owner: @ben, due: 24h)
2) Mid-term: add NX retry gating in our DNS client library to avoid immediate failover (owner: @alex, due: 7 days)
3) Long-term: root-cause with registrar + add secondary authoritative provider (owner: @priya, due: 30 days)

alex: I'll open JIRA tickets. Ben — can you give me the exact debounce config you recommend so I can include it in the ticket?

ben: Here are the quick patch knobs I tested:
```
# gslb config
health_check.debounce_ms = 5000
health_check.failure_window = 3
```
This prevented failovers in my local replay.

ops-bot: JIRA created: INF-3245 (GSLB debounce), INF-3246 (DNS client gating), INF-3247 (Registrar follow-up).

priya: Ownership confirmation: INF-3245 -> ben, INF-3246 -> alex, INF-3247 -> priya.

julia: Additional item: TLS handshake SNI mismatches were observed in 2% of failed handshakes. Ben to add extra logging to LB tls-proxy (owner: @ben, due: 48h).

ben: Will do. Patch will be rolled to canary tomorrow. @sre-oncall please watch the LB metric: lb.tls.handshake_errors and lb.routing.fallback_count.

sre-oncall: Ack — will monitor and alert on 10% spike over baseline.

alex: For the DNS client gating, proposed pseudocode to avoid immediate failover:
```
if (dns_response == NX && recent_success_count > 0) {
  retry_backoff(); // exponential, up to 3 retries
  mark_as_transient();
} else if (no_answer or SERVFAIL) {
  backoff_longer();
}
```
I'll include in INF-3246.

priya: Registrar engagement: I'll ask for logs and ask them to check for DDoS mitigation spikes. If they confirm, we escalate SLA.

julia: Recurrence analysis — this pattern matches two prior incidents (2025-11-02 and 2025-12-18) where short TTLs + transient NX caused repeated failovers. We should add a runbook note and change default TTL expectations for critical LB records.

alex: Runbook note added to infra runbooks repo and linked in each JIRA.

ben: Timeline recap — debounce patch to canary: 24h, DNS client gating PR: 7d, registrar SLA escalation: 30d. I'll post updates in this thread after each milestone.

priya: Thanks all. I'll coordinate registrar comms and infra firewall checks. :thumbsup: 

julia: Adding a recurring incident pattern ticket INF-3248 (cross-region-dns-recurrence) to track long-term mitigation roadmap.

ops-bot: INF-3248 created and linked to INF-3245, INF-3246, INF-3247.

ben: Quick note — temporarily bumping health-check log level to DEBUG on canary to capture SNI / handshake contexts.

sre-oncall: Saw the initial canary logs — will report anomalies in #eng-sre.

alex: closing loop: please ack on this thread when you've completed your assigned items so I can mark them done in the postmortem tracker.

julia: Acknowledged, will mark once INF-3245 is verified in staging.

priya: Acknowledged.

ben: Acknowledged — patch merged to canary.

sre-oncall: Acknowledged — monitoring windows active.

ops-bot: Postmortem status: 3/4 in progress, 1/4 complete. Next sync in 48h.
